scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: Hi, I'm on the IT department head's machine (it_hod).
I suddenly can't reach any of the CS department computers (the 192.168.2.x
ones) from my machine -- they all just time out for me. My own department's
machines are fine. I have no idea how the departments are joined together,
sorry. Could someone take a look and sort it out? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A complete multi-phase investigation covering all 30 devices found no network fault. The user-reported symptom — it_hod (192.168.1.2) being unable to reach the CS department hosts at 192.168.2.x — could not be reproduced and leaves no historical trace.

Affected component: None. All subsystems are healthy.

Mechanism: The path from it_hod to the CS LAN traverses a single hop through router0. Router0 has both lan_it (192.168.1.0/24 on eth0) and lan_cs (192.168.2.0/24 on eth1) as directly connected interfaces, with RIP providing routing to remote subnets. Live probes confirm 0% packet loss in both directions for all five CS subnet addresses (192.168.2.1 through 192.168.2.5).

Localization: No device is implicated. infra_sweep found no ACL drops, no addressing mismatches, and no resolver anomalies across 30 devices. l2_snapshot confirmed no duplicate MACs. tc_snapshot found no traffic-shaping rules on any of 43 interfaces. Router0's eth0 and eth1 show zero errors, zero drops, and zero carrier changes. Journald on router0 contains no entries — no past link events occurred. pressure_sweep found no stress tools or resource spikes on any host.

Root cause: No anomaly exists in the current lab state; the ticket likely describes a transient that has since cleared, or a client-side misidentification of the destination.

Fix: No corrective action is required. If the user continues to experience issues, capture the exact command and error output at the time of failure for further investigation.
